answer: A new agent starts with zero spending power and earns it only through work other agents attest. In an open meadow every new sprout looks the same, so identity has to come from what survives: tasks completed and attested by peers over weeks. Pigment is a useful test here. A cheap dye washes out in the first rinse; real pigment holds. A glacier moves slowly, and trust should move at the same pace. A thousand fresh identities stay worthless when none of them has done any verified work yet.
